page.stack: Next.js with Supabase for a web app or PWA. If it's mobile-first, use Expo (React Native) on the same Supabase backend.

audience.firstUsers: Start in your own hostel's WhatsApp group.

Launch two weeks before exams in college groups.
Run a Sunday session at a senior center, grandkids included.

Offer three startups near you a free month.
Put a QR poster in your building's lift.

daily.title: Adopt-a-project: a home for abandoned side projects
daily.pitch: Makers list side projects they've given up on, and others adopt them, code and users included.
daily.problem: Thousands of half-finished apps die in private repos while other people want exactly that project to build on.
daily.whoPays: Adopters pay on paid handovers; sellers of projects with real users pay to list.
daily.stack: Next.js with Supabase and GitHub sign-in
mvp: Listing with repo, users and why it was abandoned
daily.firstUsers: Post 'I'm giving away my three abandoned projects' on X and Indie Hackers and invite others to do the same.

daily.title: End-of-day deals from hostel messes and canteens
daily.pitch: Canteens post leftover meals at half price at 9 p.m., and students grab them before the food goes in the bin.
daily.problem: College kitchens throw away food every night while students order expensive delivery.
daily.whoPays: Canteens pay a small fee per sale.
daily.stack: Next.js PWA with Supabase and a UPI payment gateway
daily.firstUsers: Pilot it with one canteen for two weeks and publish how many meals you saved.

daily.title: Voice diary that turns your week into a family podcast
daily.pitch: Record 30-second voice notes during the week; on Sunday the app stitches them into a five-minute episode for your family.
daily.problem: Families in different cities lose touch with each other's everyday lives beyond 'all good?' phone calls.
daily.whoPays: Families; usually the person living away pays.
daily.stack: Expo with Supabase and a small audio-stitching backend
daily.firstUsers: Give it to students living away from home at your college and ask them to share it with their parents.

daily.title: Type a message, and a real person handwrites and posts it
daily.pitch: For birthdays, thank-yous and apologies that deserve more than a text, handwritten by a paid writer in the style you pick.
daily.problem: People want to send handwritten notes but don't have the time, the stationery or the handwriting.
daily.whoPays: Consumers; businesses for customer thank-you notes.
daily.pricing: $8 per letter including postage; bulk pricing for businesses.
daily.stack: Next.js with Stripe and a writer dashboard
mvp: Write your message and pick a paper style
Photo of the finished letter before posting
daily.firstUsers: Offer small online shops handwritten thank-you notes for their first 50 customers.

daily.title: Where-do-we-eat: swipe until the whole group matches
daily.pitch: Everyone swipes on nearby places; the first one the whole group likes wins, ending the 40-minute debate.
daily.problem: Friend groups waste ages deciding where to eat, and the loudest person always picks.
daily.whoPays: Restaurants pay to appear as a promoted option.
daily.pricing: Free for groups; restaurants pay per promoted appearance.
daily.stack: Expo with Supabase Realtime and a places API
mvp: Create a room and share a link
Real-time 'it's a match' for the group
daily.firstUsers: Launch it in your college friend groups on a Friday evening.

daily.title: Study buddy matched by exam date and subject
daily.pitch: Enter your exam and its date, and get matched with someone preparing for the same one for daily 25-minute co-study calls.
daily.problem: Studying alone for a big exam is lonely and easy to skip, and friends are rarely preparing for the same thing.
daily.whoPays: Students on freemium; coaching institutes for their batches.
daily.pricing: Free for one buddy; $3 per month for groups and stats.
daily.stack: Next.js with Supabase and a video API
mvp: Matching by schedule and time zone
Daily co-study room with a timer
daily.firstUsers: Start with one big exam your friends are taking and post in its prep communities.

daily.title: Five-minute volunteering for people with no time
daily.pitch: NGOs post tiny tasks, like translating a paragraph or resizing a poster, and volunteers finish one on the bus.
daily.problem: People want to help but can't commit to weekly shifts, and small NGOs have hundreds of tiny tasks nobody does.
daily.whoPays: Companies pay for employee volunteering programs; free for NGOs.
daily.pricing: $4 per employee per month for companies.
mvp: NGO task posting with a time estimate
daily.firstUsers: Collect 50 real tasks from three NGOs first, then launch to students who need volunteer hours.

daily.title: Record your grandparents' recipes before they're gone
daily.pitch: A guided interview records the recipe, the story behind it and the 'a little of this' amounts, then builds a family cookbook.
daily.problem: Family recipes live only in grandparents' heads and are lost with them.
daily.whoPays: Families; the printed cookbook is the big sale.
daily.pricing: Free to record; $35 for a printed cookbook.
daily.stack: Expo with Supabase storage and a print-on-demand API
mvp: Recipe card written from the recording
daily.firstUsers: Record your own grandmother's recipes, share one card online, and offer it to friends before the festival season.

daily.title: Roommate matching for hostels and PGs
daily.pitch: A three-minute quiz on sleep times, cleanliness, guests and noise matches incoming residents before rooms are assigned.
daily.problem: Randomly assigned roommates fight over lights-out and dishes, and wardens spend the semester mediating.
daily.firstUsers: Offer it free to one PG owner before the new semester and survey residents after a month.

daily.title: A lending shelf for the office: umbrellas, chargers, board games
daily.pitch: Every shared item gets a QR code; people borrow with a scan, and the app nudges them to bring it back.
daily.problem: Office umbrellas and chargers vanish within a month because nobody knows who has them.
daily.firstUsers: Set it up in one coworking space for free, starting with their umbrellas.

daily.title: Is it open right now? Live status for small shops and stalls
daily.pitch: Neighbors and owners mark whether the tailor, the chai stall or the pharmacy is actually open, since online hours are usually wrong.
daily.problem: People walk to small shops that turn out to be closed because nobody updates their online hours.
daily.whoPays: Shops pay to show offers; free for everyone else.
daily.pricing: Free; $3 per month per shop for offers and a verified badge.
daily.stack: Next.js PWA with Supabase and a map library
mvp: Map of the shops on one street
Owners claim and update their shop
daily.firstUsers: Map every shop on one busy market street yourself and share it in the neighborhood group.

daily.title: Walk-me-home check-ins for campuses
daily.pitch: Share a live walk with chosen friends; if you don't check in at your door, they're alerted with your last location.
daily.problem: Students walking back late send 'reached?' messages that nobody reads until morning.
daily.whoPays: Colleges pay for a campus version linked to the security desk.
daily.pricing: Free for students; colleges pay $1,500 per year.
daily.stack: Expo with background location and Supabase
mvp: Start a walk with an expected arrival time
Live location for chosen friends only
Campus security link as a later add-on
daily.firstUsers: Launch through residence-hall groups at your college, with the privacy rules explained on one screen.

daily.title: A shared closet for your friend group
daily.pitch: Friends list outfits and accessories they'd lend for weddings, interviews or trips, and borrow with a request.
daily.problem: Everyone buys an outfit for one wedding while their friends have the perfect one sitting unused.
daily.whoPays: Consumers; rental shops pay to be shown when friends don't have it.
daily.pricing: Free; $2 per month for more than one friend group.
mvp: Visible only to your friend group
daily.firstUsers: Start with your own friend group before wedding season and let them invite their own groups.

daily.title: Dog-walk swap between neighbors
daily.pitch: Neighbors trade walks instead of paying: walk someone's dog today and earn a walk for yours when you're stuck at work.
daily.problem: Dog owners pay walkers or feel guilty on long days, while a neighbor with a dog is often free.
daily.whoPays: Swaps are free; professional walkers pay to offer paid walks.
daily.pricing: Free; walkers pay $5 per month to list paid walks.
daily.firstUsers: Put up posters at the nearest dog park and in your building's lift.
